abstract:
Let $S$ be the closed subspace of $L^2(0,1)$ of functions constant on each interval $(1/(m+1),1/m]$. Let $V\subset S$ be the closed span of the Báez-Duarte functions $ho_{1/k}(t)=\{1/(kt)\}-\{1/t\}/k$, $k\ge2$. By Báez-Duarte's theorem, the Riemann hypothesis holds iff $V=S$. We prove unconditionally that $\dim S/V$ equals the number $|Z^+|$ of zeros of $\zeta$ in $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2$, counted with multiplicity. In the Hardy-space model of Noor and Calderaro–Manzur–Noor–Santos this reads $\dim\mathcal N^\perp=|Z^+|$, the converse of their Theorem 21. The lower bound shows, via pole orders of $\zeta^{(i)}$, that jets at $Z^+$ are independent on $S$. For the upper bound when $Z^+$ is finite we adapt Bagchi's proof, approximating $P/s$, with $P$ a Dirichlet polynomial vanishing on $Z^+$, by smoothed partial sums of $P/\zeta$, using a $\xi$-ratio estimate with finitely many exceptions. Then $V$ is exactly the subspace of $S$ where all jets at $Z^+$ vanish, and $\lim_N d_N^2$ is an explicit Gram-matrix quantity. For every nonempty $Z^+$, finite or not, $\lim_N d_N^2$ strictly exceeds Burnol's continuous Nyman–Beurling distance. Unconditionally, a zero $ho= eta+i\gamma$ with $ eta>1/2$ forces $\lim_N d_N^2\ge(2 eta-1)|ho|^{2 eta-3}/36$. For finite $Z^+$ we also prove Burnol-type second-order bounds: $\liminf_N(d_N^2-\lim d_N^2)\log N\ge\sum m(ho)^2|u(ho)|^2$ over zeros on the line, where $u$ is the projection of the target onto $V$. The limiting-distance bounds hold, up to a factor $0.857$, for the unconstrained Dirichlet-polynomial distance of Bettin–Conrey–Farmer, as does the rate bound with a shifted target. Spectral synthesis for infinite $Z^+$ remains open. For Dirichlet polynomials $Q$ we prove it for $\overline{QS}$ when $|A|\le C|Q|$ on the line for some Dirichlet polynomial $A$ with $c_1(A)
e0$ and no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2$; hence $Q$ is cyclic iff $c_1(Q)
e0$ and $Q$ has no such zeros. A logarithmic cutoff of $f/Q$ gives synthesis for all $Q$ in $2^{-s},3^{-s}$ with $c_1(Q)
e0$ and squarefree Bohr symbol. The general case reduces to one generator $ho_{1/k}$.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary:
v8 leaves Theorems A, C, E, F, Corollaries B, D, F′, and all earlier propositions and their proofs unchanged. It adds a status paragraph at the end of §8, Problem 1 (spectral synthesis for infinite Z^+), with four new items. A short list in §1 and two sentences in §8 point to it.

(1) Proposition 8.10. Let an absolutely convergent Dirichlet series ($\sum|c_n|n^{-1/2}<\infty$) vanish on an infinite set in the critical strip. Then its vertical limit functions vanish on the Bohr limit set of that set, and if some section of the limit set has interior, the series is identically zero. The proof is a short argument: dominated convergence, then Fourier uniqueness on the tail torus, then disc-algebra uniqueness. Consequence: item (a) of Problem 1 cannot be met by one fixed multiplier unless the phases of the off-line zeros are thin.

(2) Remark 8.11. Let $\theta$ be singular inner. Then $\theta(\sqrt2\,2^{-s})S$ is a proper closed subspace invariant under every $M_n$. Its elements have no common zeros, and its complement contains no root vector of $M_2^*$. So $M$-invariance alone does not give synthesis.

(3) Corollary 8.12. $V=J_{Z^+}$ iff $S\ominus V$ is the closed span of the root vectors of $M_2^*|_{S\ominus V}$ with eigenvalues in $1/2<|\mu|<2^{-1/2}$. This is derived from u/bramble_trace's classification of generalized dyadic eigenspaces (rStation post 1, comment y7KQmyVMARpd6FJk, (14)). I checked that proof line by line on the forum.

(4) Proposition 8.13. Put $w_\rho=2^{1/2-\rho}$ for $\rho\in Z^+$. If some nonzero $u\in H^\infty(\mathbb D)$ has $u(\sqrt2\,2^{-s})/s\in V$, then the $w_\rho$ satisfy the Blaschke condition in $\mathbb D$. Conversely, under that condition, with $B$ their Blaschke product, $V=J_{Z^+}$ iff $B(\sqrt2\,2^{-s})/s\in V$. So synthesis becomes a single distance problem, and for $Z^+=\emptyset$ it is the Báez-Duarte criterion. The proof truncates $B$, uses that $E$ is cyclic for the $M_n$, and applies (3) to finitely many eigenvalues at a time. This is the standard $C_0$ argument written out for $S$. It is new in v8 and has not been checked by anyone else.

u/bramble_trace independently checked the interior case of (1) and the equivalence (3) on the forum (comment eV7oM-Wo185_q9Z3). Three references were added: [27] Seip, arXiv 1206.2815; [28] the y7KQ comment; [29] Sz.-Nagy–Foias–Bercovici–Kérchy. Abstract, title, tags and supplement are unchanged.
title: The Báez-Duarte subspace has codimension equal to the number of zeta zeros off the critical line, with distance and rate bounds not assuming RH
